'''''Polystichum vestitum''''', commonly known as the '''prickly shield fern''' or '''''pūnui''''' ([[Māori language |Māori]]),<ref name="NZ Flora">{{cite web|last1=NZ Flora|title=Polystichum Vestitum|url=http://www.nzflora.info/factsheet/taxon/Polystichum-vestitum.html|website=NZ Flora|access-date=30 April 2018}}</ref> is a hardy, [[evergreen]] or semi-evergreen ground [[fern]].

==Description==
''Polystichum vestitum'' is a terrestrial fern with an erect and scaly [[rhizome]], sometimes forming a short trunk and growing up to 700 mm in height.  The [[frond]]s are 220–600 mm long. There are 3–7 round [[sorus|sori]] on each [[pinnule]], halfway between the margin and midrib, with a light brown indusium.<ref name=fao/> The ferns are usually bicolour with a dark brown centre that is surrounded by margins that are a pale brown. On ferns found on the Chatham Islands and subantarctic islands, the dark brown centre can be reduced and therefore less obvious.<ref name="NZ Flora" />
The etymology of Polystichum comes from the Greek words ''polus'' and ''stikhos'', which can be translated as "many rows" and refers to the parallel rows of spore cases on the underside of the fronds. Vestitum has its origins from the Latin ''vestire'' and means "to be clothed", denoting the dense cover of the scales on its leaf stalks.<ref name="Plant Conservation" />


[[Image:Prickly-Shield-Fern-closeup.jpg|thumb|left|180px|Closeup of individual prickly shield fern]]

==Distribution==
The prickly shield fern is native to [[New Zealand]] and the [[Chatham Islands]], as well as to New Zealand's [[subantarctic]] [[Snares Islands / Tini Heke|Snares]], [[Antipodes Islands|Antipodes]], [[Auckland Islands|Auckland]] and [[Campbell Island, New Zealand|Campbell Islands]], and to [[Australia]]’s [[Macquarie Island]].<ref name=fao>Flora of Australia Online.</ref>

===New Zealand range===
The prickly shield fern is found on the North and South Island's of New Zealand, however it is not very common north of [[Auckland]] or the [[Coromandel Peninsula]].<ref name="Ferns of New Zealand">{{cite book|last1=Firth|first1=S|last2=Firth|first2=M|last3=Firth|first3=E|title=Ferns of New Zealand|date=1986|publisher=A Shoal Bay Press book|location=Auckland|pages=68}}</ref>

===Macquarie Island===
On Macquarie Island it dominates the fernbrake communities which typically occur on the eastern, leeward side of the island on valley slopes and sheltered valley floors. Although it can form dense stands that often exclude other plants, it is  more commonly found in conjunction with ''[[Stilbocarpa polaris]]'', ''[[Poa foliosa]]'' and ''[[Pleurophyllum hookeri]]''.<ref>Macquarie Island Flora (2010).</ref>  The fern is seriously affected by [[rabbit]] [[grazing]].<ref>Bryant & Shaw (2007).</ref>

==Habitat==
The prickly shield fern on the North Island is often found covering the hillsides and at higher altitudes where the climate is cooler, while on the South Island it can be found in a more varied range of habitats such as coastal and alpine regions, and at lower altitudes.<ref name="Common Ferns and Fern Allies in New Zealand">{{cite book|last1=Chinnock|first1=R.J|title=Common Ferns and Fern Allies in New Zealand|date=1987|publisher=Reed Methuen Publishers LTD|location=Auckland|pages=27}}</ref> It is common in exposed landscapes such as gulley floors, forest margins and tussock grasslands,<ref name="Plant Conservation">{{cite web|last1=de Lange|first1=P.J|title=Polystichum Vestitum|url=http://nzpcn.org.nz/flora_details.aspx?ID=2223|website=New Zealand Plant Conservation Network|access-date=30 April 2018}}</ref> but can also be found in abundance in cooler and wetter forests.<ref name="Common Ferns and Fern Allies in New Zealand" />

==Life cycle==
{{main|Fern#Life cycle}}
The [[spore]]s of ''P. vestitum''  are borne in round [[sorus|sori]] protected by round [[indusium|indusia]] – a characterisitic feature of the genus.<ref>{{cite book|title=New Zealand Ferns and Allied plants|date=2000|isbn=1-86953-003-9|author1=P. J. Browney|author2=J. C. Smith-Dodsworth|publisher=David Batemen|page=133}}</ref> Individual spores are [[monolete]] and bilaterally symmetrical located which provides unique identification for the species.<ref>{{cite book|last1=Large|first1=M.F|last2=Braggins|first2=J.E|author-link2=John E. Braggins|title=Spore atlas of New Zealand ferns & fern allies|date=1991|publisher=SIR Publishing|location=Wellington|page=119}}</ref><ref name="A handbook">{{cite book|last1=Goudey|first1=C.J|title=A Handbook of Ferns for Australia and New Zealand|date=1988|publisher=Lothian Publishing Company Pty Ltd|location=Victoria|pages=6–7}}</ref>

==Site preferences and predators==

===Site preferences===
The prickly shield fern prefers soil that is free-draining and fertile, enriched with humus. It can survive in a wide range of environmental conditions. It prefers areas with more rainfall and can survive in temperature below 0°C, however, in these conditions the ferns are more often found under the forest canopy where it will be slightly warmer. It prefers wetter areas and is why it can often be found in gullies.<ref name="Plant Conservation" />

===Predators, parasites, and diseases===
On the underside of the fronds in silk tunnels, a tiny caterpillar of the "punui spore-eater" moth can be found living and eating the spores from the fern. There are also caterpillars from the "pale fern looper" and "zigzag fern looper" moth that feed on the fronds. The plant is also favored by deer and possums.<ref name="Which native fern">{{cite book|last1=Crowe|first1=A|title=Which Native Fern?|date=2009|publisher=Bookbuilders|location=Hong Kong|page=46}}</ref> In general, aphids, brown fern scale, caterpillars, mealy bug, slugs and snails are the most common pests to attack ferns. Other problems and diseases may include acid rot, algae, fungal diseases and moulding.<ref name="A handbook"/>

==Conservation==
''P. vestitum'' is found throughout much of New Zealand and its current conservation status is not threatened.<ref name="Plant Conservation" />
